scams.name: Da Nang Airport (DAD) Fake-Grab & Post-Midnight Taxi Scam
scams.description: Da Nang's airport is a common arrival point for Hue, Hoi An, and central Vietnam beach tourism — and has the same 2025-documented fake-Grab pattern as Hanoi Noi Bai and HCMC Tan Son Nhat. r/DaNang 'Airport Grab Experience' (comments/1pzsurd, 2025) gives the 2025 community baseline: 'Grab from any major Vietnamese airport is 100x easier than from Suvarnabhumi or Don Muang' — Grab IS the defensive default. r/DaNang 'What to scams to look out for in Hoi Ann' (comments/1k18dh6, 2025) documents the specific DAD warning: 'Use Grab at the Danang airport and make sure you get in the correct car. The taxis sitting at the rank are often unofficial copycats. r/DaNang 'Can I take a taxi from the airport to the city at night?' (comments/1bn4cum, 2024) documents the late-night variant: after midnight, legitimate Grab/taxi supply drops, scammers emerge. r/DaNang 'Grab taxi from Da nang airport to Hoi Ann' (comments/1k189nz, 2025) gives the 2025 Hoi An corridor baseline: 'The going rate for Da Nang to Hoi An is 250k. You probably can't get that on the Grab app' — legitimate Grab rate to Hoi An is 250K–350K VND; anything quoted over 700K VND at the airport for Hoi An is overcharging. For central Da Nang, the legitimate fare is 100K–150K VND by Grab/Be, 150K–200K VND by licensed Mai Linh or Vinasun taxi. For older travellers, the playbook: (1) book Grab or Be yourself on airport Wi-Fi AFTER you have your luggage; verify licence plate matches the app; (2) use only licensed Mai Linh (green, 1055) or Vinasun (1900-1055) on the meter; (3) for late-night arrivals (after midnight), pre-arrange hotel transfer via your accommodation's official booking; (4) IGNORE every person in arrivals offering 'taxi' or 'Grab' — all are unauthorised; (5) for Hoi An, legitimate Grab 250K–350K VND, licensed taxi 350K–450K VND — anything over 700K is overcharging.
scams.avoidance: Book Grab or Be yourself on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage — verify licence plate Use only Mai Linh (green) or Vinasun licensed taxis with meter For late-night arrivals, pre-arrange hotel transfer via official booking Typical fare: 100K–150K VND Grab to Da Nang centre; 250K–350K VND to Hoi An IGNORE every person in arrivals offering 'taxi' or 'Grab'
scams.location: Da Nang International Airport (DAD) arrivals hall and pickup zones, late-night arrivals, post-midnight taxi queue

scams.name: Ba Na Hills Cable Car Winter / 'Ruined My Trip' Scam
scams.description: Ba Na Hills is Da Nang's famous hilltop resort (Golden Bridge, French Village, cable car), but it has a specific 2025 scam genre around weather and tour-package misrepresentation. r/VietNam 'One destination ruined the whole trip. (Ba Na Hill is a scam in Winter months)' (comments/1hk0reg, 2025) is a named 2025 first-person anchor: 'TLDR: Ba Na Hill and tour guide scammed my fam' ily during December visit where the entire mountain was fogged out, cable car operated anyway, and tour guide insisted on the full-price package despite zero visibility. The scam patterns: (1) hotel-concierge tour packages at $80–$120 per person bundling the 1,150,000 VND cable-car ticket plus 'guide' plus 'lunch' plus transport for a day at the summit — legitimate direct cost is $50–$70; (2) winter months (Dec–Feb) frequently have 95%+ fog coverage at the summit; tour operators don't disclose this and don't offer refunds when visibility is zero; (3) 'express ticket' upsells at 2x the 1,150,000 VND general rate claiming 'skip the queue'; (4) independent tour touts at Da Nang street corners quoting 'best Ba Na deal' that turns out to be kickback-driven. r/VietNam 'Scam? Something else?' (comments/1cpdoqb, 2024) documents a related pattern: jade figure 'discount' scams at $55 USD for items worth $2-5. For older travellers considering Ba Na Hills, the practical playbook: (1) buy the Ba Na Hills combo ticket (1,150,000 VND / $45 USD adult, includes cable car + Alpine Coaster + Fantasy Park) DIRECTLY at banahills.sunworld.vn; (2) check weather forecast: visit Mar–Nov for reliable visibility; skip Dec–Feb unless forecast shows clear; (3) if using a package, book via Klook or GetYourGuide (all-in $60–$80 with transfer, better cancellation); (4) NEVER book via a hotel 'partner tour' at $80+; (5) at the summit, skip the $15 'foreign-artist-photo' setup and the $25 'souvenir jade' shops — both are heavily marked up.
scams.avoidance: Buy Ba Na Hills combo ticket DIRECT at banahills.sunworld.vn ($45 USD adult) Visit Mar–Nov for reliable visibility; skip Dec–Feb unless forecast shows clear For packages, use Klook or GetYourGuide ($60–$80 all-in with transfer) NEVER book via hotel 'partner tour' at $80+ At summit, skip $15 photo-setup and $25 'souvenir jade' shops — heavily marked up
scams.location: Ba Na Hills cable car entrance, Ba Na Hills tour-package bookings via hotels, weather-dependent December-February visit window

scams.name: Marble Mountains Jade & Souvenir Shop Pressure Sales
scams.description: Marble Mountains' pagoda-and-cave complex is a legitimate tourist highlight, but the adjacent jade/marble-souvenir shops run a distinct pressure-sales scam. r/VietNam 'Interesting experience at the Marble Mountains in Da Nang' (comments/193vmix, 2024) documents the pattern: tourists are funneled into specific shops by 'tour guides' (real or fake), and shopkeepers apply intense pressure to buy 'hand-carved marble' pieces at 5-10x their actual value. r/TravelDaNangHoiAn 'Visiting Marble Mountains in Da Nang – What to Know' (comments/1lzpti1, 2025) is the 2025 community guide confirming the pattern. The scam variants: (1) tour guide recommends a specific 'family-run' souvenir shop at the bottom of the mountain — they receive kickbacks of 30-50% on sales; (2) 'hand-carved' marble pieces at $50–$200 are actually machine-produced replicas worth $5-15 from the same factory; (3) 'jade necklaces' at 500K+ VND are often resin or low-quality serpentine, not real jade; (4) 'free tea' offered to soften resistance before the pitch; (5) after purchase, aggressive 'you paid cash, no refund' policies if you try to return. r/DaNang 'Marble Mountains is a must Visit!' (comments/1ofpada, 2025) confirms the site is genuinely worth visiting — the scam is in the adjacent shopping, not the monument itself. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) buy your entrance ticket (40,000 VND adult, 2025) at the OFFICIAL booth; (2) skip ALL souvenir shops at the base — they're kickback-driven; (3) if you want a genuine marble/jade souvenir, visit the artisan workshops at Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village (5 km from Marble Mountains) where prices are posted and quality is verified by the Vietnam Handicraft Association; (4) NEVER buy jade on impulse — genuine jade has a distinctive cold feel and passes a 'flashlight test' (translucent when backlit); (5) decline 'free tea' in souvenir shops — it's the social-pressure hook.
scams.avoidance: Buy entrance ticket (40K VND adult) at OFFICIAL booth only Skip ALL souvenir shops at the base — kickback-driven For genuine marble/jade, visit Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village (posted prices, verified quality) NEVER buy jade on impulse — verify with flashlight test (translucent when backlit) Decline 'free tea' in souvenir shops — social-pressure hook
scams.location: Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) cave-temple complex, jade/marble souvenir shops at the base, Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village near the mountains

scams.name: My Khe / An Thuong Beach 'Where Are You From?' Tea Scam
scams.description: A specific 2025 Da Nang scam targets solo or couple tourists on My Khe Beach and in the An Thuong backpacker district. r/DaNang (Where are you from couple in An Thuong…what is' (comments/1jrd6sn, 2025) is a named 2025 anchor documenting the pattern: a 'friendly local couple' approaches with the stock opener 'Where are you from?,' invites tourists for 'tea at our family home,' and ends at a shop selling overpriced 'traditional Vietnamese tea,' 'medicine herbs,' or 'silk scarves' at 3-5x market rates. r/VietNam 'Just landed in Vietnam Da nag' (comments/1clgoly, 2024) captures the variant context: 'It's very cheap and likely a scam. Did very same trip couple of weeks ago it cost 800k VND' — the pattern is cheap enough to not feel ruinous but adds up if repeated. The scam is particularly effective on older travellers who value the 'authentic local interaction' framing. The specific patterns: (1) couple approaches with 'where are you from?' on a beach walk; (2) invitation to 'tea at our home' that turns out to be a shop; (3) 'traditional medicine herbs' at $20–$50 that are common cooking spices worth $2-5; (4) 'family silk weaving' demonstration ending in sales pressure; (5) 'special tea tasting' that arrives with a 500K VND bill for 3 cups. r/VietNam 'Approached by someone doing a tourist survey in Hoi An' (comments/1jf2joj, 2025) documents the regional variant: 'After living in Vietnam, if anyone approaches you and speaks English well, it's a scam or' commissioned tout. For older travellers on a Da Nang beach visit, the practical defence: (1) NEVER follow a 'friendly local' home or to a 'family business'; (2) say 'không, cảm ơn' firmly and keep walking; (3) if engaged in small talk, disengage once you sense a pivot to 'come see' or 'let me show you'; (4) buy silk scarves only at fixed-price shops in the Han Market or at Dong Do Silk (posted prices); (5) buy tea only at verified shops in the Da Nang Markets with visible prices.
scams.avoidance: NEVER follow a 'friendly local' home or to a 'family business' Say 'không, cảm ơn' firmly and keep walking when engaged Disengage from small talk the moment it pivots to 'come see' or 'let me show you' Buy silk at fixed-price Han Market or Dong Do Silk with posted prices Buy tea only at verified shops in Da Nang Markets with visible prices
scams.location: My Khe Beach promenade, An Thuong expat-friendly backpacker area, tourist-hotel perimeter streets, late-afternoon and evening beach approaches

scams.name: Dragon Bridge Weekend Fire Show Pickpockets
scams.description: Da Nang's Dragon Bridge fires water and flame from its dragon head every Saturday and Sunday at 9 PM — a free show that draws 20,000+ spectators and creates exactly the conditions opportunistic pickpockets exploit. r/DaNang 'Dragon Bridge (Cầu Rồng) Saturday and Sunday at 9:00' (comments/1q4iubb, 2025) is the 2025 community reference on the show. r/DaNang '📷 Da Nang' (comments/1qaz45q, 2025) captures the 2025 escalation: 'Scams are now becoming rampant all across Da Nang' — the dense crowd at the bridge is a specific target. r/DaNang 'Don't like Danang 2026' (comments/1qbqqxr, 2025) documents the 2026 trend view: 'Scams are increasing in Da Nang. This is due to the locals now realizing there are an incr' easing number of foreign tourists. The weekend-evening crowd pattern: dense bridge-side pedestrians pushing toward the railing as the dragon's head begins to roar; phones held high to photograph; bags slung loose for the crowd pressure. The combination is perfect for lift attempts. For older travellers, the practical defence: (1) zipped crossbody bag in front during the Dragon Bridge show; (2) never carry a phone in-hand — use a wrist strap if you must photograph; (3) arrive 30 minutes early to secure a viewing spot at the bridge railing rather than pushing through crowds at 8:50 PM; (4) the show lasts 15 minutes (9:00–9:15 PM); post-show crowd disperses quickly toward the restaurant district — don't linger at the bridge; (5) for a less-crowded alternative, view from the An Thuong promenade on the opposite bank — still great angle, fraction of the crowd; (6) file report at Da Nang Tourist Police (24 Tran Phu, +84 236 3860 444) within 24 hours for insurance.
scams.avoidance: Zipped crossbody bag in front during Dragon Bridge Sat/Sun 9 PM show NEVER carry phone in-hand — use wrist strap if photographing Arrive 30 min early to secure spot at railing; avoid pushing through at 8:50 PM Post-show (9:15 PM), leave quickly rather than lingering at the bridge Alternative: view from An Thuong promenade across the river (less crowded)
scams.location: Dragon Bridge (Cầu Rồng) on Saturday and Sunday evenings at 9 PM during the fire-breathing show, riverside crowd along Tran Hung Dao Street, food-stall perimeter during the show

scams.name: Da Nang Self-Drive Rental Car Damage Scam
scams.description: Da Nang is a common starting or ending point for cross-Vietnam rental-car trips. r/DaNang 'Thoughts on renting a car in Da Nang?' (comments/1al0ks4, 2024) and r/VietNam 'Renting a self-drive car in Danang' (comments/13tfc8x, 2024) document the 2024 baseline: driving in Vietnam is challenging for tourists, and the rental-damage-claim scam is documented. r/VietNam 'Vietnam car rental advice - pickup Hanoi drop-off in Da' (comments/1b0qtha, 2024) captures the cross-country rental variant complexity. The 2024-2025 scam patterns: (1) post-return damage claims for pre-existing scratches not documented at pickup; (2) 'fuel gauge not full' demand at return despite photo evidence; (3) one-way drop-off 'cleaning fee' at the destination shop; (4) 'insurance upgrade' at 2-3x the online rate; (5) hotel-recommended 'local' rental shops with kickback arrangements and quality issues. r/DaNang '17 Scams in Vietnam to Avoid' (comments/1n50brt, 2025) confirms rental-car scams are on the 2025 community list. For older travellers considering a self-drive experience, the practical playbook: (1) SKIP self-drive entirely — Vietnamese traffic is extreme for international drivers (scooters weaving, no lane discipline, unfamiliar signage); (2) for the Hai Van Pass scenic drive, use a private-car-with-driver service via Klook at $50–$80 one-way Hue-Da Nang or Da Nang-Hoi An, or an Easy Rider pillion motorbike trip ($50–$80/day) where you ride behind an experienced local driver; (3) if you must rent, use Motorvina or Tigit Motorbikes (established operators with English-language contracts, clear damage-documentation photos); (4) at pickup, video a walk-around narrating all visible marks; (5) at return, video the returned vehicle; (6) dispute post-return damage claims with credit card chargeback within 48 hours using photo/video evidence.
scams.avoidance: SKIP self-drive — use private car-with-driver via Klook ($50–$80 one-way) Or use Easy Rider pillion motorbike trip ($50–$80/day, experienced local driver) If you must rent, use Motorvina or Tigit Motorbikes (English-language contracts) Video walk-around narrating visible marks at pickup AND return Dispute post-return damage claims with credit card chargeback within 48 hours
scams.location: Da Nang airport rental desks, city-centre rental offices, Hai Van Pass and Golden Bridge self-drive rentals, one-way Hanoi-Da Nang or Da Nang-HCMC rentals
